title: Recover interrupted record transactions without guessing or replaying decisions
statement: The system shall establish the verified outcome of an interrupted supported record transaction without guessing or replaying actor decisions, preserving committed and unrelated work and requiring explicit actor selection when recovery involves a choice of engineering effect.

what.problem: An interruption can leave incomplete publication; guessed repair or replay against newer state can create decisions never supplied by the actor or overwrite unrelated work.
what.desired_outcome: An operator obtains an exact attributable terminal state or a safe recovery stop while retaining enough valid information for subsequent recovery.

why.rationale: Recoverability must protect both recorded engineering meaning and acknowledged successful work.

stakeholders: Engineers and reviewers operating on recorded engineering work
Engineering agents acting on explicit actor decisions
Maintainers and consumers of the published command-line interface

conditions: When supported transaction interruption is detected or an actor requests recovery of unresolved publication.

contexts: The selected interrupted transaction and its verified supported recovery basis; operational backup restoration remains SR-075.

how.approach: Allow storage-engine recovery to establish an already determined committed or uncommitted transaction outcome without choosing new engineering effects. If exact completion versus restoration is an exposed supported choice, require explicit selection and verify the corresponding prepared/before state. Stop on untrusted or unknown recovery information and never replay semantic edits against newer work.

how_much.scope: Interrupted supported operational transactions only, distinct from Baseline recovery and backup restoration. Deterministic storage recovery is not authority to select a new decision, infer workflow progression, convert old formats or overwrite foreign content. MOD-011 owns ordinary engine recovery; explicit whole-store replacement follows the separate maintenance contract.

acceptance_criteria: Unavailable, corrupted, unsupported or unrecognized recovery information causes an explicit safe stop; foreign or newer work is not overwritten through guessed repair.

Where explicit completion or restoration is supported, completion reproduces the exact prepared candidate with applicable fresh basis checks and restoration reproduces the verified before-state; neither replays actor operations or edits external basis subjects.
Committed success cannot be rolled back as interruption repair. Recovery of uncommitted creation preserves all preexisting and externally added content.
Interruption during recovery remains attributable and repeatable without duplicate semantic effects; an unverified terminal state is never reported as complete.

Automatic storage recovery may only establish the transaction outcome already determined by the supported storage contract. Ordinary reads never choose completion versus restoration, import history or apply a new actor decision. An unresolved choice requires explicit recovery selection.
constraints: Current allocations and source-observed facets describe v4 SQLite. Source availability does not establish passing execution, project adoption or requirement satisfaction; historical v3 contribution arguments retain their original subjects.
